name: Hyderabad Regional Ring Road

route.end: Choutuppal, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana (northern section)

timeline.event: Northern half approved as a national highway project
Land acquisition nears completion and the northern section is redesigned as a six-lane expressway
The Centre clears the revised northern section and NHAI invites fresh construction bids

history: The Regional Ring Road is planned as a second, much bigger circle around Hyderabad, far outside the existing 158 km Outer Ring Road. The full loop of roughly 350 km would tie together the towns and highways all around the city, giving long-distance traffic a way past Hyderabad without coming anywhere near it. Only the northern half — about 161 km from Girmapur near Sangareddy to Choutuppal — has been approved; NHAI will build it as national highway 161AA, and construction bids were invited in 2026. The plan was upgraded from a four-lane road to a six-lane access-controlled expressway before any construction began, which pushed the cost up sharply. The southern half is still waiting for final approval. The map here shows the northern section.
facts: Planned as a roughly 350 km ring around Hyderabad — more than twice the length of the existing Outer Ring Road.
The northern section (about 161 km) runs from Girmapur near Sangareddy to Choutuppal via Narsapur, Toopran, Gajwel and Bhuvanagiri.
Links the big highways out of Hyderabad, including the Mumbai, Nagpur, Warangal and Vijayawada routes.
The southern half of the ring is still at the planning and approval stage.
The northern section carries the national highway number NH 161AA.
It was redesigned from four lanes to six before construction, which roughly doubled the estimated cost.
It is being built as a greenfield road — a brand new alignment through farmland rather than a widening of any existing road.
significance: Hyderabad has outgrown its Outer Ring Road: the ring that was once countryside is now city. The Regional Ring Road is meant to draw the next line, far enough out that lorries from Mumbai, Nagpur, Warangal and Vijayawada can cross the region without touching the city, and close enough that the towns around Hyderabad get pulled into its economy. Telangana expects new industrial parks and townships to follow the road, just as they followed the Outer Ring Road.

futureUpgrades: The southern half of the ring, roughly 190 km from Choutuppal back to Sangareddy, is planned but not yet approved.
Radial roads are planned to connect the new ring with the existing Outer Ring Road.
